analysis.evidence: Pharaoh and his household are the objects of the verb. The cognate phrase נְגָעִים גְּדֹלִים, “great plagues,” specifies how Yahweh struck them.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a Piel wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with יַהְוֶה as its subject.
Proper noun, masculine singular, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.morphology: Hebrew direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

evidence.note: שָׂרֵי פַרְעֹה identifies the men who see Sarai as Pharaoh’s officials.
מֶלֶךְ מִצְרָיִם identifies Pharaoh as king of Egypt.

article.name: פַּרְעֹה
article.summary: Pharaoh is the royal title by which the text names the king of Egypt. In Abram’s time, Pharaoh’s officials see Sarai and praise her to him.

draft.change: Add a name entry for the royal title פַּרְעֹה and correct the supplied gloss “lye; potash” for this occurrence.
draft.definition: Pharaoh, the title used to designate the king of Egypt.
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:15 identifies Pharaoh through his officials and his household. Exodus 6:11 explicitly calls him פַּרְעֹה מֶלֶךְ מִצְרָיִם, “Pharaoh king of Egypt.”

analysis.evidence: אֶת marks Pharaoh as the direct object of וַיְנַגַּע. Yahweh afflicts Pharaoh with great plagues, and וְאֶת בֵּיתוֹ extends the affliction to his household.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun used as a royal title, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: The king of Egypt, designated by his royal title.

analysis.evidence: נְגָעִים is the cognate accusative of וַיְנַגַּע, naming the plagues with which Yahweh struck Pharaoh and his household. The masculine plural adjective גְּדֹלִים agrees with it, giving the phrase “great plagues.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural absolute common noun with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In נְגָעִים גְּדֹלִים, “severe plagues,” the adjective describes how severely Yahweh afflicted Pharaoh and his household.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural absolute adjective modifying נְגָעִים and agreeing with it in gender and number.
